claims.statement: ExecutionEngine.executeTask enforces a fixed preflight governance order: in-memory/durable duplicate and running-state guards, execution_recovery_hold and deep_agent_assurance_hold metadata checks (throwing EXECUTION_RECOVERY_REQUIRED / DEEP_AGENT_ASSURANCE_HOLD), a pending execution-only approval check, a runtime-governance isAllowed check that cancels the task when the assigned agent is quarantined or circuit-breaker-tripped, loop/agent/attribution asserts, the admitRuntime admission gate (RUNTIME_NOT_ADMITTED), then CommandRiskClassifier.assessTask, PolicyDecisionService.evaluate, and GovernanceGateService tightening before queueing the task.

CommandRiskClassifier screens commands against ordered regex tiers (critical patterns and outside-workspace writes recommend deny; high and medium mutation patterns recommend require_approval; read-only patterns recommend allow) and is fail-closed: an unrecognized command defaults to MEDIUM risk with require_approval, never allow.

CommandRiskClassifier.assessTask elevates risk for sensitive keywords and local opencode execution, treats review_only tasks as low risk, defers to classify() when task.metadata.requested_command is present, and forces recommended_decision to deny whenever the resulting risk level is CRITICAL.

PolicyDecisionService.evaluate loads enabled approval_policies ordered by priority DESC then created_at DESC, applies the first matching policy, compiles policy match_pattern through ReDoSGuard (dangerous or invalid patterns never match), overrides to deny when the tool is in the policy's blocked_tools, and falls back to the classifier's recommended_decision when no policy matches.

GovernanceGateService is default-off (GOVERNANCE_GATE_ENABLED=true arms it), looks up OpenMythos benchmark evidence by task agent_id then nightly:<model> from GOVERNANCE_GATE_MODEL_MAP then metadata subject_model, returns allow when no evidence exists, and when the latest score is below the floor returns require_approval with a trend and optionally flagRetirement after three consecutive below-floor declining runs — it only ever tightens allow to require_approval and never loosens a deny or approval outcome.

GOVERNANCE_GATE_FLOOR defaults to 3, calibrated for a 0-5 score scale while observed openmythos_eval_runs.overall_score values range roughly 0-95, and floor() accepts any finite non-negative value (a former <=5 clamp was removed), so operators must set the floor explicitly when arming the gate or it only catches near-zero runs.

ToolBroker.evaluateToolCall rate-limits per principal (100 requests per 60s sliding window plus 10-per-second burst, throwing RateLimitExceeded), defaults to deny for unknown tools, escalates allow to require_approval at or above require_approval_above_risk (default HIGH), blocks self-allow after more than 5 allow decisions by the same principal on a task within one hour (separation of duties), and persists every decision with an immutable dec-<uuid> decision id in tool_broker_decisions.

ToolBroker capability tokens issued on allow are durable rows in tool_broker_capability_tokens scoped to category:tool, task, and principal with a 900-second default TTL; validateCapabilityToken requires tool, task, and presenting principal to all match and deletes expired tokens, and reevaluateOnParameterChange deletes the original token and re-runs the full evaluation when parameters change.

CLI executors do not mediate their internal tools through ToolBroker, so constructing a broker in ExecutionEngine does not enforce per-tool policy; callers must call evaluateToolCall before execution and validateCapabilityToken at the effect boundary themselves.

ApprovalService.createApproval stamps expires_at with approvalTtlMs() (APPROVAL_TTL_MS, default 1 hour, clamped to 5 min .. 7 days) and writes the approval row plus its canonical APPROVAL_REQUESTED audit entry in a single immediate transaction, so a failed audit insert rolls back the approval; only after commit does it schedule the off-by-default Telegram push, broadcast APPROVAL_REQUESTED over WebSocket, and call recordDecision (recordAuthorityEvent + enqueueEvent ledger/outbox records), and a failed notification is logged but never undoes the decision.

ApprovalService.decideApproval runs in an immediate transaction, rejects decisions on expired approvals (persisting expiry and audit before throwing APPROVAL_EXPIRED), enforces self-approval prevention at the data layer by throwing SELF_APPROVAL_FORBIDDEN when decidedBy equals requested_by, and refuses to process a non-pending approval twice.

Approval expiry is realized lazily on read or on a decision attempt, and realize-expiry cancels a task still in awaiting_approval (guarded so tasks that moved on are untouched) with its own task_cancelled_after_approval_expiry audit row, mirroring what a denial does.

Manual-action approvals (metadata.manual_action: true, created via POST /api/approvals) never gate or resume execution: getLatestPendingForTask with executionOnly filters them via a json_type(metadata, '$.manual_action') != 'true' predicate before LIMIT so a newer manual review cannot hide an older execution gate, and handleApprovalDecision records their decisions as evidence and returns without dispatching.

Each approval lifecycle step is mirrored best-effort (never blocking the approval) via recordDecision to the append-only authority_events ledger with a sha-256 payload digest and per-correlation sequence, and to the event_outbox as djimitflo.approval.* events that are only enqueued when EVENT_PUBLISH_ENABLED=true and drained later to the external DJIMIT_EVENT_BUS_URL.

ExecutionEngine.hasApprovedStart treats an approval as a valid execution grant only if it matches the executor kind, is not a manual action, has not expired, and its stored executionInputHash equals a fresh sha-256 hash of the task's dispatch-relevant fields — so any edit to title, description, tags, or instructive metadata, any executor-kind change, or expiry forces a new approval before dispatch.

executeTask revalidates admission after the runtimeConcurrencySemaphore capacity wait: the execution input hash must be unchanged and risk classification, policy evaluation, and gate assessment run again, with a tightened outcome aborting via EXECUTION_POLICY_DENIED or EXECUTION_APPROVAL_STALE rather than dispatching on stale authority; a granted approval resumes by re-entering executeTask.

AuditService is a façade over ComplianceAuditService: record() maps AuditEventCreateInput to appendEntry, deriving outcome from the event type (denied/violation to denied, failed/error to failure, else success) and defaulting actor to system, while both read and write the same audit_events table.

ComplianceAuditService.appendEntry hash-chains every audit_events row: previousHash is the latest entry's hash (or 'genesis'), hash is sha-256 over canonical JSON with deeply sorted keys, chain_sequence is MAX+1, SQLite triggers on audit_events and the compliance_audit_log view raise errors on UPDATE/DELETE making the log append-only, and verifyChain replays the chain checking linkage and recomputed hashes.

AuditAnchoringService computes a Merkle root over the compliance_audit_log hash chain and delivers it to a configured webhook or SIEM endpoint with exponential-backoff retries and a persisted dead-letter queue; a confirmed anchor means HTTP acceptance only (not WORM retention or remote verification), and retry timers are process-local.

Runtime admission is a distinct pre-policy gate: executeTask calls admitRuntime(taskId, executorKind) after the runtime-governance allow check and before risk classification, returning denied as RUNTIME_NOT_ADMITTED for an unadmitted runtime; admitRuntime reads the observed version only from Djimitflo's own runtime_contract_probes probe (never task metadata or runtime output), records every decision on the task and a runtime_admission policy_violation, and honors RUNTIME_ADMISSION_MODE=shadow as the operator rollback that records the denial but lets the run proceed.

The repo-held RUNTIME_ADMISSIONS ledger evaluates each runtime@version across eight gates plus authority ownership with a deterministic decide(): a FAIL on a critical gate (licensing, reproducibility, supply_chain), self-attestation, RUNTIME/SHARED ownership of any authority, or capability_gap NONE always wins; a PASS without evidence_refs is demoted to NOT_PROVEN; and checkAdmission binds the admission to the probed binary version and expires_at, with LEGACY_ADMITTED reserved for incumbents under an explicit, expiring migration plan.

createApproval merges loopApprovalLink() into the approval metadata at creation, snapshotting loop_run_id and lease_id from the worker task's metadata plus goal_id and improvement_id from the loop_runs/goals join, so the approval to run to goal to improvement link survives a mutable task row; it is empty for non-loop tasks and fail-soft (never throws).

recordDecision()'s actorType() records the decider as human only for a real users-table row, agent:... as agent, and everything else (including autonomy:* rule deciders and system) as service, so automated and inherited approvals can no longer masquerade as human in the authority_events ledger.

A retry or evolve sibling never inherits a human approval by default: inheritableApproval() (APPROVAL_INHERIT_ENABLED=true only) requires an earlier approved, non-autonomy:*, non-inherit:* decision on a maker of the same loop run with identical executionInputHash, same-or-lower risk, same executorKind/executionMode/workspacePath target, and freshness within APPROVAL_INHERIT_TTL_MS (default 2 h), and the caller records the inheritance as decided_by 'inherit:<original id>'; separately, LOOP_REVIEWER_APPROVAL_INHERIT=true lets a lease-bound checker/security_checker inherit its run's human-approved unexpired maker approval.

AuthorityGateService.authorityGateForGoal is a goal-start gate for the LoopDaemon reading the same authority_events ledger: AUTHORITY_GATE=off is a no-op, on observes (emitting a DENY event but allowing), and enforce is fail-closed — a goal without a PLAN_APPROVED/DEPLOYED ALLOW record, a missing authority_events table, or a gate error is refused, and every refusal is first appended to authority_events with a sha-256 payload digest and per-correlation sequence.

The outbound-guard wraps the process-global fetch and refuses any request to a host in OUTBOUND_DENY_HOSTS (comma-separated, case-insensitive) before a socket is opened with OUTBOUND_DENIED, shadow-logging each refusal to policy_violations; it covers only Node global fetch (not child processes, whose network egress the runtime-admission containment gate marks NOT_PROVEN) and is installed at server start under the operator rule that the VPS never calls the workstation.

services/egress-classification.ts is shadow-only reporting, not an enforcement point: classifyDestination() maps a recorded llm_model_calls row (provider URL or named provider) to local/eu_hosted/us_cloud/unknown, and checkProviderRoutingV2 plus egressEvidence only report what a stricter private_only/on_premise_only routing rule WOULD block — nothing is wired to block or reroute a call.

AUTHZ-F6 closes two write doors where a principal reached authority it does not hold — PUT /self-improve/telegram-identities/:id rejects mapping a Telegram id to a user holding permissions the caller lacks (TELEGRAM_MAPPING_ESCALATION, since the bot mints the mapped user's JWT and could have granted approve:task), and POST /segml/federation/receive no longer accepts fleet-wide peer-pattern writes with mere read:evidence.

GovernanceGuardService is the skill-deployment counterpart of the governance gate, not part of the task execution spine: runBenchmarkCheck runs an OpenMythos eval for a skill using a structured tool taxonomy and blocks deploy when the run is evidence-incomplete or scores below BLOCK_THRESHOLD 3.0/5.0 (warning below 4.0), emitting governance:guard:blocked|warning|approved, with GOVERNANCE_GUARD_MODE=disabled turning it off.
